newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila's forex reserves down to $11.7 bln.
newsitem.headline: Manila's forex reserves down to $11.7 bln.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank said on Monday its gross international reserves had gone down to $11.7 billion from a record of $12.25 billion as of March 17.
In recent weeks the Central Bank had to sell dollars and raise its interest rate to defend the peso from speculation arising from the economic crisis in Thailand.
The Central Bank said in a statement the latest level was at a comfortable three months of import cover but it was still the lowest in the region.
It said its planned Yankee bond issue would quickly beef up its international reserves to ride out any potential financial crisis triggered by unexpected events here and abroad.
Malaysia has reserves of about $27 billion which is equivalent to 3.4 months of imports; and Thailand, about $38 billion or 5.4 months of imports, the Central Bank said.

"The ongoing currency problem in Thailand underscores the need for a respectable level of reserves that provide a buffer over and above the country's normal foreign exchange requirements," the Central Bank said.
It added it planned to proceed with its Yankee bond issue when market conditions were favourable.
The Central Bank had planned to launch up to $1.0 billion in Yankee bonds in April but it postponed the sale because of poor market conditions.
